title: Judge hears testimony in death of Calgary man
article: A fatality inquiry into the death of Calgarian James Hammond was held Friday in Canmore Provincial Court.

Hammond collapsed in RCMP custody one year ago after being arrested for allegedly stealing a vehicle. He was taken to Foothills Hospital intensive care unit where he died Sept. 8, 2002. Blood tests conducted at the hospital were positive for marijuana and cocaine.

Judge J.D. Reilly heard testimony at the hearing Friday. He will issue a report establishing the cause, manner, time, place and circumstances of Hammond's death. His report, which could take several months to be released, may make recommendations on the prevention of similar incidents, but will not establish legal responsibility for Hammond's death.
